title: Flat Tag Identity Delivery
summary: migrate namespaced canonical tags and their references to globally unique flat IDs while retaining one scalar registry group
content_html:
Flat Tag Identity Delivery

Complete Result

Studio reads, assigns, creates, edits, deletes, promotes, and demotes canonical tags using globally unique flat IDs such as moss. Every tag retains exactly one scalar group such as subject.

No canonical source, assignment, alias rule, service contract, route, or analysis behavior parses the tag ID to recover group. Group-dependent behavior continues by resolving the scalar group from the registry. Registry labels and descriptions remain available, including the results of manual collision editing, so Tag-document linking can transfer descriptions into documents.

The transitional registry record after this delivery is:

{
  "tag_id": "moss",
  "group": "subject",
  "label": "moss",
  "description": "<temporary document seed content>",
  "updated_at_utc": "<timestamp>"
}

Migration Gate

Before mechanical migration, verify that every current label is globally unique. Any remaining labels with more than one namespaced registry row require manual resolution before IDs are rewritten.

For each collision, decide:

  • the resulting flat tag_id and its one group;
  • the combined or rewritten registry description retained for document seeding;
  • assignment references that collapse to the flat ID;
  • alias targets and historical selection context; and
  • whether any genuinely different concept needs a genuinely different name.

Keep the reviewed decisions inspectable until exact reconciliation proves that the proposed flat IDs are unique and all references have one intended target. Do not infer unresolved outcomes from matching labels or descriptions.

In Scope

  • Change canonical registry identity from <group>:<slug> to one globally unique normalized tag name.
  • Require exactly one scalar group on every registry row and reject a groups array.
  • Preserve registry label, allowed-group policy, the canonical tag-group taxonomy source, and group-derived configuration.
  • Preserve one registry description per resulting tag as temporary semantic source for Tag-document linking.
  • Migrate canonical series and work assignment references without changing their record shape, series-first ownership, or override semantics.
  • Migrate alias targets and historical selection context; preserve one-target- per-group constraints by resolving target groups through the registry.
  • Update first-class create, edit, rename, delete, promotion, demotion, validation, transaction, rollback, activity, and manual-patch behavior.
  • Replace every group-prefix parse with a registry lookup while retaining group selection, filtering, ordering, chips, styling, configuration, group routes, coverage/scoring, and group-derived analytics.
  • Update focused services, APIs, frontend modules, audits, checks, and tests to the flat identity contract.

Not In Scope

  • Creating, linking, editing, or publishing tag documents.
  • Adding doc_id to the registry or removing registry description.
  • Removing registry label, group policy, group taxonomy, or group-dependent UI and analysis.
  • Replacing scalar group with groups, categories, facets, senses, namespaces, or a compatibility prefix.
  • Inferring collision outcomes automatically.
  • Changing catalogue membership or the series/work assignment ownership model.
  • Adding Tag semantic-token targets.

Delivery Steps

  1. [ ] Close prerequisites and freeze the migration input. Complete Tag Vocabulary Import Retirement, then snapshot the registry, aliases, and assignments used for the cutover. Reject the input unless every tag has one allowed scalar group, every alias and assignment target resolves, and every proposed flat ID is globally unique.
  2. [ ] Change the domain contract against fixtures. Replace namespaced tag_id validation with flat slug-safe validation, validate group independently, and bump the affected canonical source versions. Change one-target-per-group alias validation to resolve each target through the registry. Keep assignment row shape, weights, inheritance, and historical alias context unchanged.
  3. [ ] Produce a read-only migration preview. Generate the exact old-tag_id to flat-tag_id map and project its effects across registry rows, alias targets, series assignments, and work overrides. Report pre/post counts, merges, unresolved references, duplicate outputs, and preserved group/label/description values. Apply nothing until the preview reconciles cleanly.
  4. [ ] Update mutation and HTTP contracts. Make create accept flat tag_id and scalar group as separate values; make promotion use the alias key as the flat ID while retaining its separately chosen group. Update edit, rename, delete, promotion, demotion, preview, apply, activity, rollback, and manual-patch paths without weakening their current cross-file planning or atomic-write guarantees.
  5. [ ] Update browser consumers. Remove prefix parsing from registry, aliases, assignment editing, and series reporting. Continue to require one group choice for creation and promotion, and preserve group filters, chips, ordering, alias constraints, coverage, and scoring by using registry group data.
  6. [ ] Perform one code-and-data cutover. Apply the reviewed registry, aliases, and assignments projection with the corresponding service and browser changes. Do not introduce a dual-read mode, compatibility IDs, or prefix aliases. The cutover must either replace every affected canonical source or restore the original bytes.
  7. [ ] Reconcile and close. Prove that every registry ID is flat, every tag has one allowed group, every alias and assignment resolves, no executable path derives group from an ID, and mapped effective series/work tags retain their intended weights and inheritance. Run focused model/planner/API tests, the studio-tag-smoke profile, scoped source searches, and a manual pass through Registry, Aliases, Series Tags, and Series Tag Editor before updating the durable destination documents.

Likely Authority

  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json
  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-aliases.json
  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-assignments.json
  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-groups.json
  • Studio tag runtime configuration and activity contracts
  • studio/services/tags/
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-*
  • studio/app/frontend/js/analytics-tag-*
  • Series Tags and Series Tag Editor frontend owners
  • tag consistency audits and focused registry, alias, assignment, route, and browser-boundary tests

These are inspection starting points. Confirm all consumers of namespaced IDs and all paths that currently parse the group prefix before editing canonical data.

Completion And Evidence

  • Every canonical registry row has one unique flat tag_id and exactly one allowed scalar group.
  • Registry labels and all descriptions needed by the next feature survive under the reconciled flat identities.
  • Every canonical assignment and alias target resolves to a current flat tag.
  • No executable path parses a tag ID prefix to recover group.
  • Group filters, styles, alias constraints, reports, coverage, and scoring resolve group from the registry.
  • New Tag and promotion create flat IDs while requiring one group choice.
  • Rename, delete, demotion, and assignment writes preserve their existing cross-file planning, atomic replacement, rollback, and activity guarantees.
  • Focused model/planner/API tests, route/module checks, exact canonical-data reconciliation, scoped source searches, a manual UI pass, and git diff --check support only this bounded migration.

Durable Destination

Update Tag Source Data, Tag Registry, Tag Aliases, Series Tags, and Series Tag Editor with the shipped flat identity contract.

Tag Groups remains the durable taxonomy reference. It describes the allowed groups without participating in tag identity.
